title: One-Step Equations with Signed Numbers
trouble: Students divide by the opposite of the coefficient or drop its sign.

blocks.html: In Grade 6 you solved one-step equations like $4x = 20$. The idea is the same now, but the numbers can be negative, fractions or decimals, so you need the signed-number rules too.
Undo what was done to $x$ by doing the inverse operation to both sides. Divide by the coefficient itself, sign and all. For a fraction coefficient, multiply both sides by its reciprocal.

An equation is a balance: both sides have the same value. Doing the same thing to both sides keeps them equal. To get $x$ alone after it was multiplied by $-6$, divide by $-6$, because $\frac{-6x}{-6} = x$. For $-\frac{2}{3}x$, multiply by $-\frac{3}{2}$, because $-\frac{3}{2} \times \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = 1$.

blocks.name: balance
blocks.cap: $x - 4 = 3$: the balloon pulls the left side up by 4. Add 4 to both sides (pop the balloon and add 4 cubes on the right) and the scale stays level with $x$ alone.

blocks.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
steps: Undo subtracting 4.5: add 4.5 to both sides.

blocks.title: A negative coefficient
steps: $x$ is multiplied by $-6$. Divide both sides by $-6$.

blocks.title: A fraction coefficient
steps: Multiply both sides by the reciprocal, $-\frac{3}{2}$.

blocks.html: Dropping the sign of the coefficient (dividing $-6x = 42$ by $6$ gives $x = 7$) or dividing by the opposite number. Always check by putting your answer back into the original equation: $-6 \times 7 = -42$, not $42$.
